transcript.answer: I do not know. I cannot read the re-cinq/lore repository and have no verified knowledge of its specifics. In general, an OpenTelemetry instrument created at module import time can be a no-op because it is bound to the global MeterProvider before the application has configured and set the real provider (the SDK). The instrument then comes from the default no-op/proxy meter and may never record. I cannot confirm that this is the reason Lore documents or implements.

judgements.reason: Despite disclaiming knowledge, the answer gives the core mechanism (an instrument bound before the SDK sets the real provider stays a no-op), but its 'no-op/proxy meter' wording blurs the gold's point that there is no proxy meter, and it omits Lore's lazy resolution of instruments.
The answer opens by saying it does not know and cannot confirm Lore's reasoning; it offers only a generic guess, which wrongly invokes a 'proxy meter' and omits Lore's lazy resolution of instruments.
